```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = NA)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

bayesplot::bayesplot_theme_set(ggplot2::theme_gray())
bayesplot::color_scheme_set(scheme = "brightblue")
```

Certain models allow for the definition of custom group rates.
Such models allow for a number of group rates which can then be changed according to the modelers choice.
We provide an example here with the heterogeneous version of the chain binomial model.

```{r}
# load heterogeneous version of chain binomial
hhmodel <- housepi::HouseholdModel$new("chain-binomial-heterogeneous")

# load parameter definitions  from template
hhmodel$load_param_template()

# inspect parameter definitions
hhmodel$param_defs
```

## Format dataset features

Suppose our analysis wants to explore age and gender-based effects within a household survey dataset.
We can create categorical groupings to stratify individuals based on their age, sex, etc to association individual group rates.
Current model allows for a number of group rates (use `$help()` method to learn more), among which the individual `"susceptibility"`. 
We can associate it as follows:

```{r}
# load the dataset from the housepi package
dataset <- housepi::survey

# create an age group binary variable child/adult
dataset$agegroup <- ifelse(dataset$age <= 15, "child", "adult")

# associate susceptibility group rate by column agegroup
hhmodel$add_group_rate("susceptibility", by = "agegroup")
```

Definitions will add a new parameter for each group, except from the reference group.
By the default, definition assumes the reference group to be the one with the largest number of counts.
To manually provide a `reference`, the corresponding argument should be set equal to the corresponding group value.
In order to see the effects of the group rate definitions on the model, a dataset must be imported:

```{r}
# import dataset from active field
hhmodel$dataset <- dataset

# inspect group rate definitions
hhmodel$group_rate_tables
```
By default, all group rates without a definition will be treated as equal to the reference. 
To return a group rate to its default, overwrite its definition with argument `by` set to `NA`. 
To drop all previous definitions use the method `$drop_group_rate_defs()`.

## Dependencies between covariates

In the previous example we associated group rates to a single covariate in the dataset.
In this example we show how to provide more covariates and a custom reference:

```{r}
hhmodel$drop_group_rate_defs()

# independent group rates, adult female chosen as reference
hhmodel$add_group_rate("susceptibility", by = c("sex", "agegroup"),
                       reference = list(sex = "F", agegroup = "adult"))

# show correspoding tables with independent associations
hhmodel$group_rate_tables$susceptibility
```

By the default, parameters associated to each grouping are assumed independent, i.e. the group rates is the product of the two parameters. 
To 

```{r}
hhmodel$drop_group_rate_defs()

# covariates are not assumed independent
hhmodel$add_group_rate("susceptibility", by = c("sex", "agegroup"),
                       reference = list(sex = "F", agegroup = "adult"),
                       independent = FALSE)

# show table with dependent associations
hhmodel$group_rate_tables$susceptibility
```

## Proceed with Analysis

All other commands stay the same.
We show an example with the very first definition of this vignette, which is equivalent to the following:

```{r}
hhmodel$drop_group_rate_defs()

# compact definition from list
hhmodel$load_group_rate_list(
  infectivity = list(by = "agegroup"),
  susceptibility = list(by = c("agegroup", "sex"), independent = FALSE)
)
```

The choice of non default group rates requires model recompilation, which is called automatically

```{r}
# inference with minimal setup (for didactical purposes only)
hhmodel$infer(dataset, n_steps = 10000, n_adapt = 1000, seed = 713,
              n_burnin = 1000, thin = 10, progress = 10)
```

```{r, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=6, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
bayesplot::mcmc_trace(hhmodel$traces)
```

The inference is performed with default assumptions for the prior, a log-normal prior (`meanlog = 0` and `sdlog = 3`) and log-normal proposer rule, as in [Cauchemez et al. (2009)](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa0905498). 
This can be customized at the moment of the definition of the group rate similarly to parameter (see documentation).

```{r}
# show parameter definitions used for the inference
hhmodel$param_defs
```

Finally, we can visualize the differences (e. g. for susceptibility) with respect to the reference group:

```{r, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}

library(ggplot2)

# compare inferred susceptibility group rates
results <- hhmodel$traces_results
sus_res <- results[startsWith(results$name, "sus_"), ]

ggplot(sus_res, aes(x = name, y = mean, color = "coral")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = cri_lower, ymax = cri_upper), width = 0.2)
```
